subject: computer-science
title: Digital Wellbeing: Foundations
welcome_lead: Being online should feel good — let's learn the habits that keep it that way.
meta_desc: KS3 e-safety: balance, screen time, healthy habits, footprint.
final_note: Use the screen; don't let it use you.

walkthroughs.body_html: Devices are tools. Set times for school, friends, sleep. Even short breaks every 30 minutes help eyes and posture.
Posts, likes and searches build your digital footprint. Future you (and future employers) can see it. Post like everyone is reading.
Turn off non-essential notifications. Your phone interrupts less and your focus improves.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of database normalisation?
options: To make the database look neater.
To make the database run faster.
To reduce redundancy and avoid update anomalies.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
